forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: FINAL Budget and Treasury Monitoring - Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Fuel costs 31% higher than prior year; multiple concurrent cost pressures emerging
findings.detail: Fuel costs are averaging £1.40 per litre in 2026-27 vs £1.07 in 2025-26, creating a £0.068m budget pressure. Combined with parish lighting electricity and maintenance pressures (£0.021m) and a £0.007m pay award pressure (after vacancy offsets), multiple cost lines are under pressure simultaneously. The council reports these are currently contained within budget but represent emerging inflation risk.
findings.matters: Multiple concurrent cost pressures indicate the council is absorbing inflation across multiple budget lines, reducing budget flexibility; if energy or labour costs accelerate further, buffers may be limited.
findings.figures: Fuel pressure £0.068m; parish lighting £0.021m; pay pressure £0.007m (contained but forecast)
findings.quote: There is a forecast pressure against fuel budgets of £0.068m. The average fuel price to date is £1.40 per litre, with an average price of £1.36 per litre forecast for the remainder of the year (compared to the average price paid per litre during 2025/2026 of £1.07).

findings.paper_title: FINAL Budget and Treasury Monitoring - Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Significant aged debt outstanding: £0.206m overdue by 90+ days, with 86% over 150 days old
findings.detail: As of 31 May 2026, sundry debtor aged debt totals £0.206m, with £0.177m (86%) overdue by more than 150 days. Main contributors are Housing (£0.065m), Property Services (£0.062m), Environmental Services (£0.033m), and others. The council notes debt recovery processes are underway.
findings.matters: Aged debt indicates cash collection difficulties and working capital strain; extended overdue periods suggest either weak debtor creditworthiness or collection process issues, affecting liquidity forecasting.
findings.figures: £0.206m total aged debt (90+ days); £0.177m over 150 days old (86% of total)
findings.quote: At the end of May 2026, there was a total of £0.206m outstanding debt in the system over 90 days. Much of this debt was over 150 days old (86%)

findings.paper_title: FINAL Budget and Treasury Monitoring - Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Wellbeing Lincs Responder Service contract delivering half expected income; ongoing pressure forecast
findings.detail: The contract with East Lindsey District Council was budgeted to contribute £0.077m annually. After a full year of operation in 2025-26, it delivered only £0.039m—a shortfall of £0.038m (49%). For 2026-27, a further pressure of £0.035m is forecast. The paper states this ongoing impact will be reviewed ahead of budget setting for 2027-28.
findings.matters: A contracted income source missing half its target signals demand forecasting problems or service viability issues, raising questions about income budget reliability and the council's ability to predict contracted outcomes.
findings.quote: Initial estimates of the impact of the contract on the bottom line for the Council were a contribution of £0.077m. Following a full year of the service being operational the actual contribution for 2025/2026 was £0.039m – a shortfall of £0.038m. A pressure of £0.035m is forecast for 2026/2027.

findings.paper_title: FINAL Budget and Treasury Monitoring - Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: General Fund Balance forecast to drop below agreed minimum working balance requirement
findings.detail: The council's General Fund Balance is forecast to be £1.985m as of 31 March 2027, falling below the minimum working balance range of £2.0m-£2.5m that members have agreed. The council notes this includes the £0.073m revenue deficit at Q1. Any balance remaining below £2.0m would be funded from the Budget Stability Reserve, using contingency resources to cover the shortfall.
findings.matters: A council falling below its minimum working balance has reduced financial resilience for unplanned costs or revenue shocks—a key indicator of financial stress for lenders assessing liquidity and operational flexibility.
findings.figures: £1.985m forecast vs £2.0m-£2.5m agreed minimum range; deficit of £0.073m at Q1
findings.quote: The forecast General Fund Balance as of 31st March 2027 is £1.985m (excluding carry forwards). This is outside of the range of the minimum working balance agreed by Members of between £2.0m and £2.5m

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 Internal Audit Follow up report
findings.headline: Overall audit follow-up shows only 44% completion rate, with auditors concluding the council has demonstrated 'little progress' on implementing management actions
findings.detail: Of 18 management actions due for implementation by 28 February 2026, only 8 (44%) were fully implemented or superseded. Five actions (28%) were partially implemented and four (22%) were not implemented at all. The auditors' formal assessment is that the council has demonstrated 'little progress' in implementing agreed actions.
findings.matters: Slow follow-through on audit recommendations suggests weak governance culture and difficulty translating audit findings into operational change. This affects how quickly and effectively the council responds to control weaknesses.
findings.figures: 9 of 18 actions confirmed as completed or no longer necessary (50%); 5 actions partially implemented (28%); 4 actions not implemented (22%)
findings.quote: Of the actions considered, testing found that nine actions had been implemented or superseded, five actions were partially implemented, and the remaining four actions were not implemented.
